ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha 49a7631b1ddb ('Profiling with firepit') introduced a firepit-based memory profiler into smtp-relay that contains a heap memory leak. When smtp-relay starts, the firepit profiler attaches and continuously leaks ~600MB per restart attempt, rapidly exhausting the 4GB heap. The smtp-relay process crashes with OOM, refuses all new connections on port 587, and cannot recover via supervisor restarts because the profiler re-attaches each time. This causes email-service workers to receive ECONNREFUSED on every SMTP delivery attempt, backing up the order-confirmations queue to 30,000+ messages and preventing checkout-service from sending order confirmation emails.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back smtp-relay to the previous stable commit (23dc47f86f5b or earlier) to remove the firepit profiler code and restore SMTP relay functionality. 2. Restart smtp-relay after rollback and verify it binds successfully on port 587 with no OOM. 3. Reset the email-service circuit breaker for smtp-relay dependency to allow worker threads to resume. 4. Drain the order-confirmations dead-letter queue (DLQ) by reprocessing the ~2,800 DLQ jobs once smtp-relay is healthy. 5. Monitor queue depth until it drains below 1,000. 6. If a profiler is needed in production, reproduce the firepit memory leak in a staging environment before re-deploying with appropriate heap limits and profiler isolation.
